_comment: Best measured mean q_score per task, and the run that produced it. scripts/read_run.py compares a run
against this, so a regression is caught by reading the run rather than by remembering. Update an entry only
when a run beats it on the SAME instances -- a different instance set is a different measurement. Every
number here was taken with --knowledge oracle and sticky grasping, which the challenge does not allow; they
measure the planning and motion pipeline, not a submission.
instance_count is what read_run.py compares: a run over a different number of instances is not a like-for-like comparison, however its mean turns out.

Two runs of the same code on the same two instances of putting_away_toys gave blocked-motion counts of 46 and 62 and empty-mask counts of 9 and 17. Treat a single run's counts as an observation, not a measurement.

turning_on_radio.note: ten instances; the button pose is oracle

assembling_gift_baskets.note: single instance best: 0.875 on 301 in the 2026-09-12 regression

dispose_of_batteries.note: 0.25 and 0.50; the baseline it beat was 0.25 on both (runs/bench_batteries_5)

putting_away_toys.note: 0.75 and 0.875, seven of eight toys placed in one instance, and runs/bench_toys_8 repeated it exactly. Two runs before the ramp block-test and presenting fixes gave 0.4375 and 0.375. Read scores, not mechanism counts: runs 7 and 8 are the same behaviour for this task and gave 9 against 17 rounds lost to empty masks and 46 against 62 blocked arm motions, which is this task's noise floor.
